## Load the data

```{r}
#Ensure that Data_Wrangling_LivePred.R is in your working directory
library(e1071)
```

```{r}
# Run the wrangling script. It creates the objects below in this R session.
# It also saves copies under Data/derived; it does not split or fit models.
source("R/Data_Wrangling_LivePred.R")
```

The script creates two data frames containing the same rally observations:
`score_only` and `score_plus_skills`. These include identifiers and the outcome,
so we should not pass every column directly to a model.

It also creates numeric predictor matrices: `x_score` and `x_skills`.
The separate factor `y` contains the home team's eventual `loss` or `win`.
The starting skill matrix uses cumulative counts; rates remain available in
the larger data frame for later selection and preprocessing.

```{r,echo=FALSE,message=FALSE}

# Dimensions are number of rally snapshots by number of predictor columns.
dim(x_score)
dim(x_skills)
```

## Prepare for the training/test split

```{r,echo=FALSE,message=FALSE}

# Choose scores plus skills for this SVM; use x_score for the score-only model.
svm_x <- x_skills
svm_y <- y

# Keep match IDs alongside the inputs so entire matches stay in one partition.
# Do not include these IDs as SVM predictors.
match_ids <- score_plus_skills$match_id
```


```{r}
# Make the random selection reproducible.
set.seed(303)

# List each match once, in a consistent order.
matches <- sort(unique(score_only$match_id))

# Randomly reserve approximately 20% of matches for testing.
test_matches <- sample(
  matches,
  size = ceiling(0.20 * length(matches))
)

# Identify the rows belonging to those matches.
# Both predictor matrices have exactly the same row order.
is_test <- score_only$match_id %in% test_matches

# Score-only inputs.
x_score_train <- x_score[!is_test, , drop = FALSE]
x_score_test  <- x_score[is_test, , drop = FALSE]

# Score-plus-skills inputs: use the SAME row selection.
x_skills_train <- x_skills[!is_test, , drop = FALSE]
x_skills_test  <- x_skills[is_test, , drop = FALSE]

# Both models use the same outcome labels.
y_train <- y[!is_test]
y_test  <- y[is_test]
```

```{r}
# This will fit the score-only model
svm_score <- svm(
  x = x_score_train,        # this uses the training predictors
  y = y_train,              # the y training has the known win/loss outcom
  type = "C-classification",
  kernel = "radial",         # RBF is a good standard
  cost = 5,                  # will tune this later
  scale = TRUE              # Learn scaling from training inputs
)

# Fitting the score-plus-skills model with same training as the previous but with skills
svm_skills <- svm(
  x = x_skills_train,
  y = y_train,              # Making sure to use the same outcomes and training observations as to not compare different things
  type = "C-classification",
  kernel = "radial",
  cost = 5,
  scale = TRUE
)

# this will see how the models predicted
pred_score <- predict(svm_score, newdata = x_score_test) 
pred_skills <- predict(svm_skills, newdata = x_skills_test)

# Confusing mat or something
table(Actual = y_test, Predicted = pred_score)
table(Actual = y_test, Predicted = pred_skills)

# Fraction of the test set snapshot accurately identified
mean(pred_score == y_test)
mean(pred_skills == y_test) # the skills one did perform worse than the score only #For kernel = RBF, and 
```
